name: The Second Plane of Rathauspark
verified_sources: data/registers/wien-naturdenkmale.json (Naturdenkmal register_id 3257651, city of Vienna MA22 designation, species Platanus x hybrida, place 1., Rathauspark)
data.wien.gv.at WFS layer ogdwien:BAUMKATOGD (Vienna city tree inventory, MA42, BAUM_ID 147537: PFLANZJAHR 1873, STAMMUMFANG 597 cm), fetched this pass
de.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rathauspark_(Wien) (confirms the park's 1873 founding and that several of its trees, planted as mature stock, are older than or contemporary with the park itself)
access: Free, in the public Rathauspark next to Vienna's city hall, open during daylight hours year-round.
story:
Vienna's tree register says this plane was planted in 1873. It gives that same year to every protected tree in the Rathauspark, and 1873 is when the park itself was laid out around the new town hall. That is what a register writes down when a whole park goes in at once, so the date says more about the city's paperwork than about this tree. Several of the park's trees arrived as mature stock, already grown on the day they were planted. The honest answer on age is a band rather than a year, somewhere between a century and 160 years, and nobody has counted the rings.

The trunk has been measured, and it comes to 5.97 metres around, within a few centimetres of the thickest in the park. Vienna gave it individual legal protection as a natural monument in 1973, one of three planes here to get it.

Even at the low end of that range it has stood through the annexation of 1938, the war, and the ten years of four-power occupation that followed, all of it playing out around the building it faces. The famous plane is at the front of the park with a legend and a disputed 1783 date attached to it. This one is at the north end doing the same work with none of the attention, a mottled grey column splitting into heavy limbs under a crown wide enough to shade that corner on its own.

name: The Plane of Hügelgasse

location.address: Hügelgasse, in front of no. 7, 1130 Vienna

de.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liste_der_Naturdenkmäler_in_Wien/Hietzing (address given explicitly as 'Hügelgasse, vor Nr. 7' i.e. in front of house no. 7, meaning it stands on the public street rather than in a courtyard; girth 2.2m/220cm, height 18m, crown diameter 16m; protected since 1955-01-17)
access: Free, a street tree standing in front of Hügelgasse 7, visible and reachable from the public footpath at any time.
transport: U4 Unter St. Veit, about 6 minutes' walk.
story:
Most of the protected trees in this corner of Vienna stand in private courtyards. This one stands on the pavement. Hietzing's list of natural monuments reads largely as addresses with "im Hof" after them, in the courtyard, behind a gate somebody else controls. The entry for this plane says "Hügelgasse, vor Nr. 7", in front of house number 7, which is the difference between a tree you can read about and a tree you can put your hand on.

It is not the biggest plane in Vienna and does not pretend to be. The trunk measures 2.2 metres around. What it has is a crown 16 metres across on an 18 metre frame, which on a narrow residential street means it covers the road, both pavements and the fronts of the houses on either side. In summer the whole block sits under it.

Vienna entered it on the register of natural monuments on 17 January 1955, four months before the State Treaty ended the four-power occupation of the country. It has held the same patch of pavement in Unter St. Veit, the villa quarter west of Schönbrunn, ever since.

Nobody has put an age on it. The register carries its height, its girth and the day it was protected, and nothing at all about when it went into the ground. If you know, tell us.
